info.description:
The DittoFS node's management API (RFC 23 §4), generated from the API's route table and its wire types.

- A call carries a bearer token unless its operation's security is empty. A caller whose role may not read what a call reaches is answered 404, as though it did not exist; one that may read it but not make the call, 403.
- A read that answers an ETag answers the record's tag. With ?wait=<duration>, above 0 and at most 1m0s, it is a long poll: it answers once the record changes, or once the wait passes.
- A listing answers one page: ?limit= (default 100, at most 1000) and ?after=, the opaque cursor the previous page answered as next, which the last page leaves out.
- A PUT, a PATCH, a DELETE, or a POST action that changes the spec, carries If-Match with the ETag it read, or, a PUT that may create its record, If-None-Match: *; without one it is refused 428, and with a stale one 412. A PATCH body is a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) of the PUT body: a field present sets it, and null resets it to its default.
- A POST or a DELETE carries an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key and the same request answers what the first answered, and one with another request is refused 422.
- A request body names no field its type does not have. Its schema requires no field: one left out takes its default, and a handler refuses, 400 naming it, one it needs.
- A write that starts an operation answers 202 with the operation and its Location; GET /api/v1/operations/{id}?wait= follows it.
- Every refusal is application/problem+json: its code names the refusal, and retryable says whether the same request may succeed later. Any refusal may carry Retry-After.
- The API listener also answers the health probes GET /health/live and GET /health/ready, unauthenticated and in text/plain, which this document leaves out.

Extensions on each operation: x-dittofs-role is the least role that may make the call, none for a public one; x-dittofs-role-by-kind is true when the call needs instead the role that starts the kind of the operation it names; x-dittofs-starts is the kind of operation the write starts, answered 202, and x-dittofs-may-start the kind it starts only when what it writes calls for one, answered 202 then and as its own answer otherwise; x-dittofs-waits-applied is true when the write's answer waits, at most 1s, for the node answering it to apply it.
